docs(extensions/github): fix stale webhook path

## What & why

The GitHub App setup instructions pointed the Webhook URL at `/api/v1/github/webhook`, a route quack never mounts: SDK extensions are served under their bare extension name (`/github/webhook` — `internal/server/router.go` mounts each extension at `/<name>`, the extension registers `POST /webhook`), while `internal/server/reserved.go` reserves `/api/v1` for quack's own REST/MCP routes. So anyone following the doc got a 404. The code was right; the doc was the stale side (per the plan approved on the issue: fix the doc, do not move the mount).

Closes #1147

## Spec (non-trivial changes)

Skipped - trivial docs fix.

## Checklist

- [x] `go test ./...` passes (all 35 test packages ok; docs-only change, no `-race` needed)
- [x] `make vet && make fmt` clean (`go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l internal cmd` both clean; no Go files changed)
- [x] No `openapi.yaml` change, no generated files touched

**Verification**

- `git grep -n "/api/v1/github/webhook" -- docs/` → no matches
- `git grep -c "/github/webhook" -- docs/extensions/github.md` → 5

Live check (optional; not run here — no configured local server in this environment): with a running quack that has `extensions.github` configured, `POST /github/webhook` should not 404 and `POST /api/v1/github/webhook` should.

**Ops note — no quack redeploy needed**

If a live GitHub App still has its Webhook URL configured as `https://<host>/api/v1/github/webhook`, repoint it to `https://<host>/github/webhook`: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → the App → Webhook URL, and check Recent Deliveries to confirm the 404s stop. That is a GitHub App settings change, not a quack code or deployment change.

**Related (separate repo, not part of this PR)**

fagerbergj/quack-extensions had the same stale path as the qa-mock `send` subcommand's `--url` default; fixed on `qa/github-remarkable-mocks` (`github/cmd/qa-mock/main.go`, default is now `http://localhost:8080/github/webhook`; `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` from `github/` all green).

One more edit beyond the five doc references: `docs/qa-mocks.md` quoted the stale path in a "known-bug" callout that claimed it was "tracked separately"; it is fixed by this PR, so the note now points at #1147.

feat(frontend): make the nav rail a fully collapsible overlay drawer

## What & why

Owner feedback on 0.51.x (#1145): the collapsed icon bar "uses the same icon as the chat left nav and doesn't save any space", and "I don't want an always-on icon bar either". Per the plan agreed in the issue (option a), the persistent rail is deleted — the 160px `w-40` column, the 40px collapsed strip, the sub-600px hamburger column, and the `navRailCollapsed` localStorage key — and the `fixed inset-0 z-40` overlay drawer #1145 already ships below 600px becomes the only navigation shape at every width. One new 44px toggle (own glyph, never the chat-list ☰) in each route's header leading slot opens it; it closes on selection, Esc, ✕, or backdrop tap, remembers nothing, and renders zero DOM when closed.

Closes #1171
Closes #1175

## Spec

- **Scope / out of scope** — `NavRail.tsx` rewritten as a pure drawer; new `NavToggle.tsx`; drawer state owned by `App.tsx` (always closed on load); `useCompact.ts` deleted; the three collapse stories deleted; the nav descriptions in `docs/extensions/ui-kit.md` and the frontend-design skill updated. Non-goals held: no hover-expand, no keyboard shortcuts, no per-user persistence. A second, test-only commit parallelizes the node-spawning mermaid tests in `internal/vetting`/`internal/tools` — each spawns `node scripts/mermaid-validate.mjs` (~1.4s) and none called `t.Parallel()`, so `go test ./...` ran 58s, at the edge of the 60s gate; it now takes ~19s.
- **Forbidden actions** — nothing rewrites `navRailCollapsed`; no element shares the chat-list toggle's ☰ glyph; `useMediaQuery` and the 600px `--breakpoint-medium` stay (ChatList/Chat/ChatMenu still use them).
- **Output contract** — `NavRail` takes `open: boolean` + `onClose: () => void` (keeps `route` / `activeExtension` / `initialExtensions`); `open: false` renders `null`, `open: true` mounts the overlay at every width; every tappable surface is ≥44px with `dark:` twins.
- **Test cases** — (1) fresh load with a stale `navRailCollapsed='1'` seeded: drawer closed, key neither read nor rewritten; (2) toggle opens the drawer; selection, Esc (focus returns to the toggle), ✕, and backdrop each close it; (3) exactly one ☰ exists in the DOM.

fix(frontend): compact one-pill composer below 600px

## What & why

The composer's bottom bar is ~110px + safe-area tall on a 390px phone before any text is typed (#1174). Below the existing 600px `medium` size class it now renders one compact pill; at 600px and above every element renders its previous classes byte-for-byte, so desktop is pixel-identical by construction. A second commit parallelizes the slow Go mermaid-validator tests so `go test ./...` fits the 60s gate budget (measured 60.2s → ~19s).

Closes #1174

## Spec (non-trivial changes)

- **Scope / out of scope** — `frontend/src/components/Composer.tsx`, `Composer.stories.tsx`, `Composer.test.ts`, new `Composer.rtl.test.tsx`; plus `internal/vetting/mermaid_test.go` and `internal/tools/check_mermaid_test.go` (test-only). Wrapper padding is a pure-CSS `medium:` split (unprefixed = compact); the row and queued area are `useCompact()` branches because they swap decoration/subtree. No API change, no generated files, no Go production code. Out of scope: CSS `field-sizing` auto-grow (the #425 problem), separate from this height fix.
- **Forbidden actions** — no full-text action buttons on compact (owner rule: an icon does); outline is `ring-1` (box-shadow), not a border (a border adds 2px and busts the 44px row budget); DOM elements stay mounted across the 600px crossing (only className strings swap) so the textarea keeps focus and IME state.
- **Output contract** — compact (<600px): wrapper `px-3 pt-2 pb-[calc(0.5rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]`; one `rounded-full` 44px-tall ringed row: 44×44 icon attach / `flex-1 min-w-0` textarea (`text-base` 16px, `max-h-32`, 128px grow cap) / 44×44 icon Send (or Stop between it and Send while streaming); queued messages collapse to a DOM-handled `<details>` "N queued" chip (stays open across queue additions without re-rendering; remove control always visible, no hover on touch). ≥600px: unchanged classes.
- **Test cases** — new `Composer.rtl.test.tsx` (5 cases): narrow matchMedia → 44px-floor classes on the icon Send with empty text content (name from `aria-label`); compact send submits typed text via userEvent; streaming shows the 44×44 icon Stop and Queue stays reachable; `dir="rtl"` row class string carries no physical `left-/right-/ml-/mr-` utilities and both icon buttons keep their accessible names; tapping "N queued" reveals the queued text and a remove control. `Composer.test.ts` pins the auto-grow cap at 128px (narrow stub) and 192px (wide stub).

## Checklist

- [x] `go test ./...` passes (`-race` for concurrency changes) — passes; the vetting change adds test-internal concurrency (an RWMutex the two global-mutating tests hold as writers, every validator test as a reader via `requireMermaidValidator`), which I could not run under `-race` in this sandbox (no C compiler) — CI's `make test-race` is the check

- [x] Changed `openapi.yaml`? No
- [x] No hand-edits to generated files
- [x] Comments say what the code *can't* - no narration or change history

### Acceptance coverage (real-browser step is yours)

- Empty composer ≤ 60px + safe-area at 390×844 / 360×740: 8 (pt-2) + 44 (row) + 8 (pb) + 1px preserved `border-t` = 61px by `getBoundingClientRect()` — eyeball it in Storybook (`MobileViewport`, `MobileViewport360`, `MobileViewportStreaming`) under DevTools <600px emulation, light and dark; I can't run a browser here.
- Hit targets exactly 44×44: pinned by the rtl tests' class assertions.

feat(frontend): result view for the artifact panel

## What & why

The node's artifact panel was a picker: a native `<select>` of raw ids ("text:plan (text)"), a desktop id sidebar, "Select an artifact" as the heading. Owner feedback (0.51.1 mobile): "this dialog is too technical and not helpful to users." The panel is a result view now: opening it renders the node's primary output under the node's own name, with the judge rounds as a chip timeline above it, a "Revision N of M" prev/next bar with a single diff toggle, secondary artifacts behind a labelled "More" section, and all provenance (id, kind, class, lineage, timestamps, the REST link) in a collapsed "Details" disclosure at the very bottom. No `<select>` remains anywhere in the panel; mobile is a full-height (`h-dvh`) bottom sheet with the timeline pinned under the header.

Closes #1178

## Spec (non-trivial changes)

The full spec is the approved plan comment on the issue; summary:

- **Scope / out of scope** — `frontend/src/components/ArtifactPanel.tsx` (rework), its three test/story files, the three narrow props at the `DagNode.tsx` mount, and two small `api.ts` additions (`artifactUrl`, status-aware diff error). Out of scope by design: live SSE wiring for `artifact_revision`/`artifact_judge_round` (the panel stays REST + manual Refresh), the documented latest-revision lineage gap, and per-item diff inside "More".
- **Forbidden actions** — no new dependencies; no native `<select>` in the panel; no string matching an artifact id (`kind:instance`) outside the opened Details disclosure.
- **Output contract** — `ArtifactPanel` takes `{ chatId, nodeId, nodeTask, nodeError?, nodeArtifactKind?, onClose }`. Primary output = the non-judge artifact whose kind equals `nodeArtifactKind`, else the highest `latest_revision` (tie: `lineage.saved_at`, then name). `JudgeRoundContent` gains `scored?: { artifact_id; revision }[]` mirroring `ScoredRef` in `internal/vetting/reviewrecord.go`; a chip tap jumps to that ref's revision (fallback: latest) and stamps the round's notes through the existing #1139 anchor machinery, turning the diff toggle off. `DagNode` passes the error only on a `failed` status — the same condition as the red banner — so a transient error on a running node never reads as a failure.
- **Test cases** — (a) finished plan node: one tap shows the rendered plan, `<h2>` = the node's name, both chips; tapping round 1 shows revision 1 with its note highlighted. (b) failed node, no artifacts: "This node failed before writing its result." + the error text, no timeline, no picker. (c) 4× (narrow/desktop × light/dark) matrix: no id-shaped string outside Details; opened Details is the only place id/kind/class/lineage/REST link appear. Plus diff on/off/413-degradation, prev/next at the ends, "More" inline expansion, and the three new `DagNode` props reaching the panel.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint src/ && npm test && npm run build` — all green (460 tests; the build's chunk-size note is pre-existing).
- `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` with a fresh writable `GOMODCACHE` — clean. This commit changes no Go; the branch's other commit (`5ddad6a`) carries the `DagNodeDef.artifact` wire field this panel reads.
- No browser was available in this sandbox, so visual QA is the new Storybook stories: `WithResult`, `WithResultDark`, `WithResultMobile` (390×844 box), `FailedNode`, `MoreHeavyNode` — `npm run storybook`, Chat/ArtifactPanel. Please check both themes at 390×844 and 1280 on the mobile sheet there.

## Feedback wanted

- The "More" human labels (finding → "Findings", code_review → "Review", pr_body → "PR description", document → "Document", text/bytes → "Files") are a presentation choice; finding rows show an ordinal (`#1`) because their instance is a content hash.
- Details renders its content only while open: a closed native `<details>` keeps its content in the DOM, which would leak the id to text scanning and some screen-reader modes.

## Out of scope

- Live SSE updates for artifacts (documented in the panel; follow-up of #1092).
- Node membership for revisions a later node rewrites (documented gap; needs per-revision lineage at chat scale).
- Per-item diff inside "More" items.

## Checklist

fix(home): prune sent notices after 30 days and started keys idle 90 days

Fixes #2329.

**Retention.** `notices` and `started` gain an `at` column (existing rows start their clock at the first boot with this change). Pruned on each `run.ended` the app records and on `start()`, no new timer:
- `notices`: `sent = 1` and older than 30 days. Only a restart's redelivery of an unacknowledged event needs a sent row, so 30 days is far more than enough. Unsent notices are never pruned.
- `started`: not touched for 90 days. A key is refreshed on `/started` and on each of its runs ending, because a session can run again (the issue's 'last run ended' is not knowable); an idle key is a session nobody awaits.

No approved contract covers the home app (checked the contracts list on prod's read-only API). Prod row counts are not exposed by the API (the app's `/apps/home` is 401), so not checked.

**Evidence.** Test added in `packages/home/test/notices.test.ts` with an injected clock; fails on main (no pruning), passes here. `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (1253 tests, 0 fail), sloplint ok. Not a UI or model-path change.

test(workflows): wait on the resumed run after a crash, with and without the lifecycle sender

Fixes #2392. Prod workflows do not rerun completed steps after a restart. The failure #2390 saw was a race in the test, not an effect of the task-graph observer.

## Cause

`workflows.test.ts` "a crash mid-step resumes at that step…" reopened the session and then called `runWorkflow(…, null)`. Reopening already resumes the interrupted task (`harness.resume()` in `openSession`, packages/session/src/runtime.ts:115), and `startWorkflow` (packages/workflows/src/index.ts:104-108) joins a recorded run only while it is live or when the request matches. With a null request and a run that has already finished, it starts a fresh run, and that run executes the first step again.

The test passed only because `runWorkflow` happened to run before the resumed task finished. Any extra await in `openSession`, such as #2390 mounting a started `watchTaskGraph` there, let the resumed run finish first. At the point `runWorkflow` was called, the resumed task 8 was already `terminal/completed {first: 1, second: "finished"}`, and `runWorkflow` then created task 10. Two extra reads between reopen and `runWorkflow`, with no observer at all, fail main the same way.

The observer itself is read-only. `TaskGraphView` in pi-durable 1.5.0 builds its value from task scans and commit publications and never writes, so it does not change task identity or phase order.

## What changed

The test now waits on the recorded run, and checks that the reopened session's run is the same task. It runs twice: bare, and with the lifecycle sender mounted the way `runtime/src/main.ts` mounts it, which includes the sender's task-graph watch and the `withdrawEnded` sweep. The first step appends a line to a file, standing in for a posted message, and the test asserts that line was written exactly once.

## Evidence

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npm test`: 1253 tests, 1250 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped (Postgres catalog conformance without `QUACK_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, and the two live docker driver tests); web 417 passed.
- `npm run sloplint -- diff origin/main`: `sloplint: ok`.
- With #2390's experiment re-applied (`watchTaskGraph` started in `openSession` calling `withdrawEnded`), the old test failed 3 of 3 runs with `{ first: 2 }`. Both new cases passed 3 of 3.

### Prod (read-only)

- Only `sleeper-*` and `remarkable-ingest` agents are workflow-bound; research sessions run the agent loop.
- Sleeper seals in the last 48 h were at 2026-11-17 06:15Z (digest v3, retro v1) and 09:30Z (trends v10/v11), plus 2026-11-16 09:31Z (trends v9). Deploys were at 04:55Z and 09:49Z on 11-17. No workflow run was in flight across any of the 24 deploys in that window.
- Every sealed version across the week-10 sleeper sessions and week-9 trends/retro has a distinct hash. Trends v10 and v11 are 16 s apart, and both failed their verdicts: that is a judged-step revision, not a rerun.
- Every sleeper start carries a `requestId` (`packages/sleeper/src/jobs.ts:6`), so a retried start joins the recorded run instead of taking the null-request path.

fix(qa): test the distributor relaunch loop through seams, not a real port squat

Fixes #2394.

**Cause.** The test squatted a 127.0.0.1 port and expected the distributor's wildcard `listen(port)` (`packages/distributor/src/main.ts:60`) to fail on it. That holds on Linux but not on every netstack: where the listen succeeds, the readiness probe reaches the squatter, which never answers, and `waitFor` in `startDistributor` (60 s) outlasts the test's 30 s timeout.

**Change.** `startDistributor` takes `{ next, start, serving }` seams (port source, launch, probe). The test now drives the relaunch loop with fake children: one that exits then one that serves, and three exits failing. No port, process or timer. The real-process path stays covered by the `startStack` test in the same file and the QA rig.

fix(qa): tell the stack's own distributor from another process on its port

Refs #2412.

## Cause
`startDistributor` (tools/qa/stack.ts) declared the stack ready when anything answered `/version` on the picked port. `freePort` is bind-then-release, so another stack can take the port first. Our child then dies of EADDRINUSE, but only after mounting apps and trying to listen, and the probe can already have succeeded against the other stack's distributor. If that stack has no schedules app, `GET /apps/schedules` is `404 {"title":"no such app"}`, which has no `schedules` field: the reported failure. Mount order is not the gap: main.ts awaits `mountApps` before `listen`.

## Change
- Each launch sets a `QUACK_COMMIT` nonce, which `/version` echoes. The probe accepts only that nonce, so a foreign answer is not ready, the child's exit is noticed and the existing relaunch loop picks new ports.
- The test no longer probes the freed port after `stop()`: a concurrent stack can take it (seen once in 300 parallel runs, `true !== false`). A teardown test checks the process groups directly. The status of `/apps/schedules` is asserted.
- New tests for the probe (own nonce vs foreign) and for per-launch nonces.

## Evidence
- Forcing the collision (another distributor-like server on the port handed to `startDistributor`): before, 3/3 returned the foreign server and `/apps/schedules` was 404 problem+json; after, 3/3 relaunched and got `{"schedules":[]}`.
- The natural race did not reproduce: 0/300 (20 copies in parallel x 15) plus 180 mixed stacks at 60 concurrent, on origin/main. After the fix, 300/300 pass in the same configuration.
- `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` x3 green; `sloplint diff origin/main` ok; QA rig `home-sessions,contracts` passed.

perf(judge): a pass-only any group escalates after its decision-model answers

Refs #2409. Fixes the extra judge-model requests in the #2422 replay: +19% judge time, and 27B requests 135 -> 200.

## Cause

Under `pass-only`, a decision-model "no" is never final; it escalates like an unsure answer. With inner `any`, one pass decides the group.

The engine sends every packed request at once (`index.ts:239`, on main), but the decision model takes them one at a time (`clef: limiter(1)`, `index.ts:220`; `resolve.ts:99`). Each request escalates its own unsure items as soon as its answers are in (`resolve.ts:243-247`). `need` (`index.ts:233`) only sees the answers received so far.

So in a (guarantee, part) decomposition, the pairs for the early parts reach the judge model before a later part's pass for the same guarantee arrives. Once that pass arrives, those escalations were wasted.

## Change

For a grouped check with inner `any` under `pass-only`, an unsure item waits until the decision model has answered every item of its group that it is asked. It waits outside the escalation slots, then escalates through the same `need` check, batching and limiter as before.

- If any of those answers passed, the group is decided and nothing escalates.
- If none passed, the group's items escalate, and items still queued when a judge-model pass lands are skipped.
- Decision-model requests go out exactly as before. Only escalation waits.
- Items reused from earlier rounds and items code settled are not waited on.
- A decision-model error still counts as answered, so it releases the group's items.

Inner `all` gets no hold. Under pass-only the decision model can only pass an item, and a pass never decides an `all` group (only a "no" does, and that has to come from the judge model). Waiting would delay those escalations without skipping any.

Flat checks, grouped checks without pass-only, and grouped `all` checks go through the same code path as before: `ready` returns `undefined` for them.

## Contract fit

The approved Judge evidence API v29 says a pass-only failing answer "escalates through the same path, with the same batching, the engine's existing need-based skip … and the same escalation limiter". It also says "an undecided item of a decided group is not escalated to the judge model". This change keeps all of that and changes only when an escalation starts, which the contract does not specify. If you want that timing written down, one sentence would cover it: "Under `pass-only`, an `any` group's items escalate only once the decision model has answered every item of the group, so a pass it gives decides the group first."

## Evidence

- `npm run typecheck`: ok.
- `npm test`, run twice: 1330 tests, 1327 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped (node) and 426/426 (web) on both runs.
- `npm run sloplint -- diff origin/main`: ok.
- Five new tests in `packages/judge/test/grouped.test.ts`, using the fake decision and judge models. Four fail on main:
  - A group of three Clef "no" and a last Clef pass sends nothing to the judge model. On main it sent 3.
  - An all-"no" group escalates only after its last decision-model answer, and an item still queued after the judge model's pass is skipped.
  - Two groups interleaved across three packed requests: only B, which no part passed, escalates. On main A's two "no" pairs escalated too.
  - With reuse, the group's two reused failures stand and only its fresh items are waited on. On main the fresh "no" escalated before the fresh pass.
- The fifth test passes on main as well: a decision-model error on one item of a group still releases the group, and undecided handling is unchanged.
- I did not re-run the replay. No model calls were allowed for this task, so the #2422 replay needs re-running on this branch to measure the saving.

One more finding, not changed here because it also affects flat checks: the limiter gives a slot to the next waiter before the finished escalation's answer is counted. Even at `escalations: 1`, one extra item gets through after a deciding pass.

perf(judge): a packed decision-model request states a repeated question once

Refs #2409. Clef's time grows linearly with request bytes (0.01 s + 0.263 s/KB, fitted over 67 recorded requests) and it takes one request at a time. This PR cuts bytes from packed decision-model requests.

## Change (`packages/judge/src/resolve.ts`, `request()`)

- A question asked of two or more items in a packed request is now written once, in a new `asks` list in the request state. Each of its questions reads `About items[i]: answer asks[k].`
- A question asked of only one item stays inline as `About items[i]: <instructions>`.
- The unit id is sent once, in `items[i].id`, instead of inside every question. I kept it in the item because some ids carry evidence the item state doesn't: a contracts definition's method and path exist only in its id.
- Questions keep the neutral ids `q0`, `q1`, …, no check name reaches the decision model, and answers map back by question order exactly as before.
- Lone (unpacked) requests are unchanged, and so is the judge-model prompt.
- `pack()` measures requests with the same function, so a pack now holds more items under the cap.
- `PROMPT_VERSION` goes from 1 to 2.
- Not cut: the per-question `criteria`. pi-ai's `ClassifierQuestion` type requires it.

## Bytes, model-free, same code path

I ran `replayJudge` over `~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/full-rubric-cases.json` (13 cases, whole rubric). ## Reuse cost

Bumping `PROMPT_VERSION` changes every reuse key. The first judged version of each live session after the deploy re-asks all its items once, as if reuse were off. That costs about one full fresh round per session, about 15 to 40 s per contracts version on the replay set. Old entries stay in the store, which never drops entries, and are no longer read.

## Not included

I did not reorder the decision-model queue. No property known before asking separates checks that will escalate from ones that won't: every check asked of the decision model escalates on an unsure answer. In the traces, `contradicts_guide` escalated and `meets_intent` didn't, but only because of how they were answered. "Fewest requests first" would help aab002bf (about 8 s) and nothing on 0ac788c4. feat(github): deliver checks the PR description's claims about the diff

Refs #2322.

## What changed

Until now, `deliver` checked only the backticked commands and commit ids in `artifacts/pr.md`. It now also runs `diffClaims` (`packages/github/src/claims.ts`) against `git diff --name-status`, the base and HEAD trees, and a `git grep -F -w` of the code names the text uses. A delivery fails when `pr.md`:

- names a path under one of the repo's top directories that is in neither the diff nor either tree,
- names a code name (camelCase, snake_case, Capitalized, dotted or `name()`) that no tree holds, in a paragraph or list item that says something was added, new, renamed, created, exported, removed, deleted or dropped,
- says "new `path`", "deleted `path`", "changed/updated/edited/added in `path`", or "`path` unchanged" / "no changes to `path`" when the diff did otherwise (a "no", "not" or "never" earlier in the clause skips the phrase),
- says "docs-only" while touching a non-`.md` file, or an unqualified "no Go/TypeScript/JavaScript/Python changes" while touching such a file.

Paths outside the repo's top directories (another repo, `artifacts/...` in the session workspace) and names cited in prose with no add/remove cue (dependency APIs such as `TaskGraphView`) are not checked. Each of those caused a false flag on real PRs before the restriction was added.

## Why

The issue asks for a code-only gate on the implementer's claims about its own diff, measured on a labelled set. A false flag sends a correct PR back, so the gate covers only claims a diff can settle and leaves the rest unchecked.

## Evidence

The change is code-only, with no prompt or rubric change, so the evidence is a deterministic run over a labelled set built from real PRs. The set lives outside the repo, in `~/quack-lab/implementer-claims/` (`claims.jsonl`, `planted.json`, `bin/measure.ts`). fix(chatStore): purge stale text/runs on fresh dag_plan

## What

When a fresh `dag_plan` event arrives on a LiveTurn that has accumulated top-level content (e.g. orchestrator narration from the pre-planning phase), the stale `text` and `runs` bleed into the new DAG scope. This caused GitHub-origin active runs to show no live DAG in the chat box — only the "Running" badge, with phantom top-level narrator text behind or mixed into node answers.

## Why

The `onDagPlan` handler created a fresh `DagTurnState` with empty `nodeAnswer`/`nodeRuns`, but left `live.text` and `live.runs` untouched. These accumulate during the pre-planning phase when the orchestrator emits top-level events (response_created → agent_start → agent_token) before any DAG is ready. When multiple hub dispatches replay into the same LiveTurn, or a new plan replaces prior top-level narration, the old text persists and contaminates the new run's output view.

## How

- **Hardcoded `Closes #N`** promises a full close. Combined with the pr-authoring skill also adding it to PR bodies, a **partial-fix merge auto-closed issues** they shouldn't have (#463 is a real example).

## What

Deterministic extraction of stated user preferences from mention messages before the orchestrator runs. Preferences are committed to `user:<login>` bucket via the normal `Store.Commit` path — dedup + consolidate preserved.

**New files:**
- `internal/orchestrator/message_mine.go` — preference pattern rules + mining function

**Modified file:**
- `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:297-305` — mines preferences at the start of every `Run()` when user memory is enabled

Fixes #262: per-user memory partitioning fails because qwen3.6-35b doesn't reliably call the `commit_memory` tool even when instructed in its prompt (`agents/orchestrator/memory.md`). A 9-issue plan sweep added zero memories.

Pattern (1) from the issue triage: "deterministic commit — mine the user's message for stated preferences and commit them directly." Follows the same pattern the trust gate uses to answer-mine tradecraft for coding/research buckets. No change to prompts, tools, or memory internals.

## How

`MinePreferences(message)` runs 25+ compiled regex patterns against message text:
- **Verbosity** — terse/concise/brief vs detailed/thorough (case-insensitive)
- **PR style** — open PRs / keep on branch / draft
- **Proceed vs ask** — "proceed on best judgment" vs "always ask before acting"
- **Review style** — inline comments vs high-level summaries
- **Language preference** — prefer TypeScript/Go/Python/Rust
- **Communication tone** — friendly/polite vs professional
- **Goals & limits** — explicit goal statements and test exemptions

Transient context is stripped (e.g. `[on my-project#42]`), content normalized to third-person ("User prefers..."), and each candidate goes through the normal `Store.Commit` dedup+consolidation so duplicates are skipped and updated phrasing updates rather than creates new entries.

The mining fires once per `Run()` call when `userMem != nil`. Run in a goroutine (best-effort, never blocks). Memory is available to follow-up turns via the existing recall path (`preload_memory`).

fix(config): reject unknown YAML keys at startup with rename hints (closes #560)

## What & why

`yaml.Unmarshal` silently ignores unknown YAML keys in `quack.yaml`. When a config key is renamed (e.g. `memory_role` → `memory.bucket`), deployments that drift to the old key get no signal: the server boots clean, agents run, and the feature is broken with nothing to diagnose.

This replaces `yaml.Unmarshal` with stream-based decoding using `yaml.NewDecoder().KnownFields(true)`, so any unrecognized YAML field at **any nesting level** now fails startup, naming the unknown key. For known renames (`memory_role`), a pre-scan on the raw YAML produces a migration hint: `"unknown field 'memory_role' — use memory.bucket instead"`.

Closes #560

## Spec (non-trivial changes)

- **Scope / out of scope** - In scope: KnownFields enforcement for all config keys, `knownRenames` map + pre-scan helper for migration hints. Out of scope: bulk migration tooling for existing deployments.
- **Forbidden actions** - Do not add new dependencies; keep `yaml.v3` only. Do not modify `applyDefaults()` — structural validation (KnownFields) and semantic validation (applyDefaults) remain separate concerns.
- **Output contract** - `Load()` returns an error naming the unknown field; for known renames, the error appends a replacement hint. No fields are silently ignored anymore.
- **Test cases** - unknown top-level key rejected; unknown nested key in server/workspace/gates.judge rejects; deprecated `memory_role` rejects with migration hint mentioning both old and new keys; valid config with all legal fields loads without regression; KnownFields applies at every nesting level.

fix(vetting): add format-checks to trust gate (closes #585)

## Why

The v0.16.1 re-run of #560 passed the trust gate and opened #584 — which then **failed CI on `go fmt`**. Two gaps combined:

1. **Every derived check was excused as failing-at-base** — a `--depth 1` clone lacks `node_modules`, module caches, etc., so all six derived checks (`npm run build`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `make build`, `make test`) were waived by the pre-existing-failure probe (`baseline.go`). The gate degenerated to judge-only.

2. **`gofmt -l` was never a check** — AGENTS.md tells agents "Run `make vet && make fmt`" but nothing in the trust gate enforced it. CI caught it separately via `test -z "$(gofmt -l internal cmd)"`. Fixing #583 (the probe) made this visible: all checks were individually correct to waive, leaving *nothing* deterministic between judge and delivery.

## What changed

### Format-check candidates in the derived-check infrastructure (`vetting/checks.go`)

- Added `"gofmt -l"` for Go repos (when `go.mod` + `gofmt` binary are present). Uses `skipBasePrefix` tag so the gate **never waives it** via `failsAtBase`.
- Added `"npx prettier --check --list-different"` for JS/TS repos (when `package.json` + `npx prettier` exist and the allowlist permits it). Also tagged — formatting violations cannot pre-exist on the base commit.

Format-checks use a prefix tag (`!gofmt:`) so they're distinguished from build/test checks: the prefix is stripped before execution, but `isSkipBase()` keeps them from ever reaching `failsAtBase`. The baseline waiver simply doesn't apply because gofmt/prettier output on the base tree equals the working-tree result minus the worker's edits.

### Allowlist prefixes (`config/config.go`)

- Added `"gofmt"` and `"npx prettier"` to `defaultCheckCommands` alongside existing entries like `"go build"`, `"npm run"`, etc.

### "All checks waived" warning (`vetting/checks.go`)

- After the check loop runs, if ALL derived checks were excused as failing-at-base (and there were any), emit a `WARN` line:  
  `all derived checks waived for this node; no deterministic verification ran`  
  Makes the "verified nothing" state visually distinct from "checks passed".

## How

The tag convention: `skipBasePrefix = "!gofmt:"`. Format-checks are tagged during derivation (`deriveChecks`), filtered by allowlist/toolchain using the stripped form, and the checker skips baseline for tagged commands. This is lighter than introducing a wrapper type while keeping both marked and unmarked candidates in one `[]string`.

## What

Add `UpdateChatOrigin(chatID string, origin *ChatOrigin) error` to the SDK's `Host` struct, and wire it in quack to `store.SetChatOrigin`. This lets extensions update a chat's origin (badge state) without starting a run.

## Why

Issues closed by GitHub/PRs merged/reopened still show badge 'open' in the sidebar because ChatOrigin is stamped once at dispatch and never updated after that. State-change webhooks received by the GitHub extension have no way to refresh the origin.

## How

**extsdk/** — local fork of `quack-extensions/sdk` v0.3.0 with `UpdateChatOrigin` added as a new function field on `Host`, following the same pattern as `ArchiveChat` and `Classify`:
- `extsdk/go.mod` + `go.sum` — module definition matching upstream
- `extsdk/sdk.go` — main source with the new field (same API style, doc comments)
- `extsdk/host_test.go` — added test verifying nil-degradation and callability
- `extsdk/registry.go`, `baseconfig_test.go`, `registry_test.go` — supporting files ported from upstream

**extensions.go** — wired `UpdateChatOrigin` in the Host struct construction: marshals the `*ChatOrigin` to JSON, passes it to `store.SetChatOrigin` (the same write path used at dispatch time).

**go.mod** — added replace directive so all consumers resolve github.com/fagerbergj/quack-extensions/sdk → ./extsdk/

## Verify

- `go vet ./...` — clean
- `go test ./internal/serve/...` — 14 tests pass (all SDK extension dispatch loop, registry, disabled-stays-dormant, attachment handling, bound workflows)
- `go build ./...` — full binary compiles
- `go test ./extsdk/...` — 3 tests pass (BaseConfigDefaults, Registered empty, UpdateChatOrigin nil-degrade)

## Notes for github extension follow-up

The GitHub extension (`quack-extensions/github`) needs to call `Host.UpdateChatOrigin` from its webhook handlers (issues.closed → 'closed', pull_request.merged → 'closed', pull_request.opened/reopened → 'open'). The SDK change here provides the capability; the extension-side wiring is a separate PR.

Closes #844
